The following divisibility properties hold true for any sequence defined by a recurrence of the form a(n+1) = P(a(n)), n >= 0, where P(x) is a polynomial with integer coefficients:
a(n+k) - a(n) divides a(n+k+j) - a(n+j), for k >= 1, j >= 0 (proof by induction on j).
In particular, this shows that reducing the sequence modulo D = a(n+k) - a(n) produces a periodic sequence of period k, starting at index n. An example is given below.
For m >= 1, a(n) - a(k) divides a(m*n) - a(m*k) provided a(n) != a(k).
More generally, for r, s >= 0, a(n) - a(k) divides a(r*n + s*k) - a(s*n + r*k), and
a(n) - a(k) divides a(r*n)*a(s*k) - a(r*k)*a(s*n) = det([a(r*n), a(r*k); a(s*n), a(s*k)]). (End)
